claims.evidence: Newsletter audience proof uses Anthony's supplied active Beehiiv figure of about 23,215, rounded to 23,000. The connected Drive source is application/pdf and 6,592,307 bytes. No public open-rate replacement, sponsor-performance, science, guest, member-count or wider financial claim is introduced.

editorial.evidence: The release remains a narrow P0 correction. Newsletter and partners copy preserve the existing structure and weekly-letter positioning while removing inflated 30K/30,000+ and 65% proof. The fallback route adds no promotional copy.

offers.evidence: Beehiiv posts, automations, referral configuration, coaching prices, sponsor packages, Skool and paid acquisition are unchanged. The Core Guide remains a referral reward asset and is not offered as the newsletter signup incentive.

desktop.evidence: The exact P0 page bytes were rendered in Chromium at 1440x1000 for /newsletter and /partners. The checks found 23K/23,000 present, 30K/30,000+ absent, 65% absent and no horizontal overflow. The fallback changes only the download route and restores deployment config; it does not alter those page components or styles.

pages.observations: The Saturday Spin hero, signup form, corrected 23,000-reader proof, content sections and bottom signup banner render cleanly with no 30K/65% copy or horizontal overflow.
The media-kit hero and newsletter reach cards render cleanly with 23K/23,000 reach and no open-rate percentage; the existing hierarchy and layout remain intact.

mobile.evidence: The exact P0 page bytes were rendered in Chromium at 390x844 for /newsletter and /partners. Corrected audience proof remained readable, 30K/30,000+/65% claims were absent and document width matched the viewport. The fallback does not change mobile UI.

pages.observations: The hero, form, consent copy, 23,000-reader proof, content cards and bottom signup banner remain readable without clipping or overflow.
The media-kit reach cards remain readable and the corrected newsletter figure fits the existing mobile layout without horizontal overflow.

interactions.evidence: Newsletter EmailCapture reads source and optional utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign only when query attribution is enabled, submits them through the existing /api/newsletter path, and the existing Beehiiv helper maps those values to Beehiiv UTM subscription fields. Existing fixed-source asset funnels remain unchanged. No real subscriber was created during QA.

seo.evidence: The newsletter metadata/social audience statement was corrected to 23,000 with no new search claim. The canonical download path is same-domain and stable. No new doorway page, keyword variant or sponsor marketing surface was added.

technical.evidence: The exact fallback content digest completed a full Next.js production-mode build: compilation and TypeScript succeeded, all 4,463 static pages generated, and the route table contains dynamic /downloads/core-training-guide.pdf. The route follows the Drive download, rejects any upstream body that does not begin %PDF-, and on success returns application/pdf with Content-Length, stable filename, cache headers and nosniff. vercel.json is restored to the known-good pre-P0 configuration. Final public HTTP verification is the required post-deploy smoke check, not a pre-deploy assertion.
